messages.subject: Part 4 Sleep Log Error Message
parts:
Hello, 
I am running GGIR both with and without a sleeplog as the guider to compare results to determine whether to use a sleep log for our final datasets. I was able to successfully run GGIR using the basic log format on a subset of 10 IDs, but am running into errors when I run a sleep log on all IDs. 

Here is the error I have run into when running the basic sleep log: 



The code associated with this output is attached. 


To fix this, I have 1) updated R and GGIR, 2) Ensured that the IDs match the IDs of the filenames, and 3) Double-checked that the format for the times are in xx:xx:xx format. 

When running the advanced sleep log, I run into an error message stating that a participant has missing values. The participant in question does not have missing values in either the basic or advanced sleep log.  

I am able to successfully run using HDZCA as the guider, but as mentioned above, want to compare results with output using sleep log as a guider to determine best practice for our studies. 

Thank you. 

  1. Reagan

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 4 Sleep Log Error Message
parts:
Hi Reagan,

Thanks for describing your issue. I see in your sleeplog that the date format that you have is m/d/y, not y-m-d. Can you try with the revised sleeplog attached? Please, do not open it in excel or try to define the format in excel, sometimes excel changes the format of dates in csv files and I suspect this is what occurred. 

Please, let us know if you can read the sleeplog now, maybe we need to revise the documentation regarding the format of dates or try to address these formats somehow.

Best,
Jairo
-----
In case you need it, I used this script to change the format in your sleeplog:

S = data.table::fread("Sleep log_visit 6_final.csv",
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE, data.table = FALSE,
                      check.names = TRUE, colClasses = "character")
datecols = grep("date", colnames(S))
for (di in datecols) {
  chardates = S[, di]
  dates = as.Date(chardates, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
  S[, di] = as.character(dates)
}
write.csv(S, "Sleep log_visit 6_final_jhm.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
